sentences.text: Opposite Party :- State Of U.P Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Govt. Lko.

Counsel for Applicant :- Manish Bajpai Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and Sri Rajeev Mishra, who has filed Vakalatnama on behalf of complainant and perused the record.

2. The FIR in question was lodged alleging that the daughter of the informant was harassed by the in-laws for dowry and on account of non-fulfillment of the demand of dowry, she was killed and hanged.
General allegations were levelled against all the family members, who were named as accused in the FIR.
The applicant herein is the husband of the deceased.

1 3.
The Counsel for the applicant argues that in the postmortem report, the cause of death is due to asphyxia as a result of antemortem hanging.
He draws my attention to the antemortem injuries to demonstrate that apart from the ligature mark present all around the neck, no other injury is reported.
He further argues that the mother-in-law and the father-in-law have been enlarged on bail by separate orders dated 15.06.2023 and 04.07.2023 respectively.
The applicant is in custody since 20.02.2023 and has no criminal history.
4. Learned A.G.A. as well as learned Counsel for the complainant vehemently opposed the bail prayer by arguing that the offence in question is serious in nature.
It is further argued that the marriage is less than 7 years and approximately 4 years have been passed.
They further argue that considering the gravity of offence, the applicant is not entitled for bail.

5. After hearing the Counsel for the parties, what transpires is that general allegations have been levelled against the entire family members with regard to the demand of dowry and harassment, the medical report demonstrates that the death is due to asphyxia as a result of antemortem hanging,
except ligature mark all around the neck, no other injury was found on the body of the deceased, the burden of discharge under Section 304-B IPC is to be done at the time of trial and there is nothing on record to demonstrate that the applicant if enlarged on bail, would in any way adversely affect the trial and without expressing any opinion on merit, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
6. Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

7. Let the applicant Santosh Kumar Prajapati be released on bail in FIR/ Case Crime No.45 of 2023,
under Sections 498A, 304-B IPC and Section 3/4 of D.P. Act, Police Station Ghungter, District Barabanki on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
